Show and install the programs wdx needs besides itself.

git is mandatory: projects and their terminals need it. The others are optional: without one, only the features it enables are missing.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`wdx deps install`](#wdx-deps-install) | Install a dependency with the system's package manager |
| [`wdx deps list`](#wdx-deps-list) | List the programs wdx needs, whether each is ready, and what it enables |

## wdx deps install

Install a dependency with the system's package manager.

```sh
wdx deps install --name <dependency> [--yes] [flags]
```

On Ubuntu and Debian with apt, on macOS with brew. When installing needs root, the commands are shown and you are asked before sudo runs them; sudo then asks for your password. `--yes` answers in advance; without a terminal sudo cannot ask, so it works only when no password is needed. docker and podman each provide the container dependency. A dependency already ready is left as it is. Every failure says why and how to install it yourself.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--name <dependency>` |  | dependency to install: git, clipboard, docker, podman, gh, vi, vim, nvim, nano, hx, emacs |
| `--yes` |  | run the commands that need root without asking |

- `--name` is required
- with `--json`: one of `--yes`

### Examples

```sh
# Install the clipboard tool TIDE copies with
wdx deps install --name clipboard

# Install docker without being asked
wdx deps install --name docker --yes

# From a script, where sudo needs no password
wdx deps install --name git --yes --json
```

### Output

The dependency as it is now, with what is left to do, as logging in again. With `--json`: {"result": ..., "dependency": {...}, "install": {...}}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `installed` or `ready`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`cancelled`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#cancelled) | 1 | the question was answered no |
| [`install_failed`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#install_failed) | 3 | the package manager failed |
| [`privileges_required`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#privileges_required) | 1 | installing needs root, and sudo cannot ask for the password |
| [`unsupported_system`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#unsupported_system) | 1 | wdx cannot install it on this system: the instructions say how to by hand |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx deps list

List the programs wdx needs, whether each is ready, and what it enables.

```sh
wdx deps list [flags]
```

A dependency is ready, missing, too\_old (git before 2.31) or not\_ready: installed but not usable, as docker whose daemon does not answer. The clipboard tool is the one for the session: wl-copy on Wayland, xclip or xsel on X11, pbcopy on macOS.

### Examples

```sh
# Every dependency
wdx deps list

# As JSON, for a script
wdx deps list --json
```

### Output

Each dependency: mandatory or optional, its status, the program and version found and the features it enables; why it is not ready below; then the system. With `--json`: {"system": {...}, "dependencies": [...]}

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |
